stem.en: At 20 °C, 36 g of common salt dissolves in 100 g of water. A student says, "So a saturated salt solution at 20 °C is 36 % m/m." Is the student right?

text.en: Yes, because 36 g in 100 g is 36 %.
No, it is 56 %, because 36 g in 64 g of water is the fraction to use.
No, it is about 26.5 %, because 36 g is out of 136 g of solution.
No, because a saturated solution cannot be given a percentage at all.

explanation.en: Solubility is per 100 g of water, but % m/m is per 100 g of solution. The solution here is 36 g + 100 g = 136 g, so (36 g / 136 g) × 100 is about 26.5 %. Option a is the tempting one, because it reads a solubility as a percentage. Option b mixes up the two numbers. Option d fails because any solution has a concentration.

hints.en: What is the total mass of the solution?
Use mass of solute / mass of solution × 100.
